## Headline read — the most replicable thing

Claudia operates through persistent, multi-method follow-up on long sales cycles (18–24 month dormancy gaps are normal). She surfaces grant eligibility early, anchors deals to external funding (Hone), then executes sequential check-ins tied to tangible product releases (HORIZON reports, training rollouts) rather than generic touchpoints. This turns waiting time into deal progression.

## Conversation openers

### re-engagement / existing project follow-up

**Pattern.** She reaches out around concrete product availability or event attendance. Uses personal invitation tied to customer's actual project status, not mass messaging.

**Verbatim:**
> "Just a quick note - the National Carbon Farming Conference kicks off this week in Albury... If you're heading along, let me know - we can grab a coffee or catch up for a quick chat about how your project's going."
> "Thanks for your time on the phone today. I have sent HONE an email to organise an online training with HONE devices. The HORIZON features are about to be released into the platform in the next few weeks."

### cold outbound / referral follow-up

**Pattern.** Claudia (or team on her behalf) uses warm introductions and references specific property details gleaned from first call. Positions next step as information delivery, not pitch.

**Verbatim:**
> "It was great to speak with you this afternoon about the soil carbon opportunity across you and your wife's properties. So that you have the appropriate information to recap our conversation I have attached our information pack and FAQ document."

## Discovery questions

- **Clarify eligibility constraints early (clearing history, grant fit, existing competitors). Asked conversationally on initial calls, not email.** — _surfaces:_ Reveals deal-stoppers upfront so team doesn't invest in ineligible prospects. Also frames Claudia as expert, not order-taker.
  > "Need to check clearing events don't make it ineligible."
  > "For this, we will need to check on the clearing component as cleared forest must be 5-7 years old before beginning a project."
- **Dig into property specifics: acreage breakdown, soil type, prior land management, clearing timeline, stocking rates.** — _surfaces:_ Maps property heterogeneity to project boundaries and cost estimates. Builds confidence in feasibility before formal scoping.
  > "3300 Total at Mooni, 1300 Brigilow, 2000 acres of old cultivation and rundown pasture... Rotational grazed."
  > "Taken out heaps of wattle - planted pangola. 200acre paddocks. Reasonably flat and undulating. Hard pan underneath."
- **Identify financial gatekeepers and funding sources (grants, spouse involvement, decision timeline).** — _surfaces:_ Surfaces affordability objections and co-decision-makers before they block progression. Anchors solution to grant availability.
  > "Property at Mooni - Wife inheriting from family but Tony calls the shots, wife not particularly interested in the goings ons... Hone grant of relevance."
  > "Biggest concern is cost of sampling - Hone grant of relevance"

## Transitions

### From discovery (first call) → information delivery + grant positioning

Immediate follow-up email with info pack, FAQ, and Hone grant flyer. Frames as 'so you have the appropriate information to recap'—permission to close without hard ask.

> "So that you have the appropriate information to recap our conversation I have attached our information pack and FAQ document. I'm very happy to answer any other questions that come up, reach out anytime. I have also attached the information flyer for the Hone Grant."

### From information stage → technical validation + scoping

Once customer signals interest, Claudia hands off to technical team (Bill, Kieren, Will) for title/map review, clearing verification, cost estimate. She maintains continuity by owning the customer-facing timeline and next-step communication.

> "I have sent HONE an email to organise an online training with HONE devices. The HORIZON features are about to be released into the platform in the next few weeks. When that happens, you will be able to see your soil carbon predictions for your current project."

### From waiting period (dormancy between grants, product releases, sampling) → value-add check-in

Claudia touches base around externally-timed events (conference invites, new product releases, training availability, sampling schedules) rather than arbitrary cadence. Gives customer reason to re-engage that isn't a sales call.

> "Just a quick note - the National Carbon Farming Conference kicks off this week... Our team will be there across the three days, including Tuesday's Soil Carbon Day, which we're co-sponsoring."
> "Thanks for getting that in so quickly. Kieren has confirmed that in that area you have shaded that would be considered clearing, and that area would have to wait at least 5 years (and likely 7) before being eligible for a carbon project. If you have any further questions, feel free to reach out."

## Customer archetypes — who they engaged well

### Grant-constrained grazier (primary income from livestock, cost-sensitive, co-decision-maker spouse)

**Characteristics.** Acreage 1000–3500 Ha, existing rotational grazing, improved pastures, wants carbon revenue but affordability is gatekeeper. Family succession planning involved (spouse or heir).

**Approach.** Lead with Hone grant positioning in discovery call. Provide preliminary cost quote tied to acreage early. Confirm grant eligibility and follow up with flyer and FAQ. Return periodically when grant status or sampling schedule allows re-engagement.

**Example.** Tony Castle (Mooni, 3500 Ha, wife inheriting, Hone grant critical to deal). Alan Deen (~1000 Ha, cost concerns 'worth doing?', resolved via extended discovery + HORIZON projection).

### Existing AgriProve customer (established project, seeking expanded scope or reporting upgrades)

**Characteristics.** Already sampled, has baseline carbon results, wants visibility into predictions or new paddock opportunities. Long dormancy normal (1–2 yrs). Reengages around product releases or conference attendance.

**Approach.** Touch base around HORIZON releases, sampling anniversaries, or event invitations. Offer new reports or training tied to product availability. Keep technical updates flowing (sampling schedules, results, ACCUs issued).

**Example.** Peter Ramsey (Lyne Carbon Project, sampled Sept 2023, reengaged around ACCU issuance notification, engaged with results). Tony Castle (post-project, May 2026 re-engagement around HORIZON report generation).

### Competitor-adjacent prospect (already working with similar provider, seeking integrated or dual-method approach)

**Characteristics.** Engaged with GreenCollar or Climate Friendly, interested in AgriProve soil carbon component. Typically larger operations with mixed land use (cleared/vegetated/grazing).

**Approach.** Surface early in discovery whether other providers are involved. Position AgriProve method as complementary. Don't compete on price; differentiate on technical fit (soil carbon method, grant integration, reporting).

**Example.** Tim Skerrett (wants integrated method, already with Climate Friendly; Alan Deen (GreenCollar on vegetated land, AgriProve on grazing).

### Public-facing / media-engaged farmer (willing to advocate, success story potential)

**Characteristics.** Comfortable sharing farm bio, photos, and results. Responsive to outreach from marketing team. Active in peer networks or social media.

**Approach.** Once project succeeds (ACCUs issued, visible improvement), initiate media/interview outreach. Frame as storytelling, not sales. Provide drafts for approval. Invite to Carbon Builders Facebook group and conference panels.

**Example.** Jeff Bell (interviewed for Carbon Builders bio, Oct 2024; issued ACCUs Sept 2025; reengaged by Marketing team Dec 2025 for quote material).
